differential: Cervical radiculopathy
Nerve compression in the cervical spine could cause bilateral arm paresthesias.
Thoracic outlet syndrome
Compression of nerves or blood vessels in the thoracic outlet can cause paresthesias in the arms.
Multiple sclerosis
Demyelination in the central nervous system can present with sensory symptoms like paresthesias.
Anxiety disorder
Hyperventilation associated with anxiety can cause bilateral paresthesias.
Vitamin B12 deficiency
B12 deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, leading to paresthesias.
Radial nerve entrapment
The distribution of paresthesias and wrist extension weakness points to radial nerve involvement, potentially from compression.
Cervical radiculopathy
Nerve root compression in the cervical spine could cause bilateral arm paresthesias and weakness, though the posterior forearm and wrist extension findings are more specific to the radial nerve.
Thoracic outlet syndrome
Compression of the brachial plexus in the thoracic outlet could cause paresthesias and weakness in the upper extremities.
Brachial neuritis
This inflammatory condition of the brachial plexus can cause pain, weakness, and sensory changes in the upper extremities.
Multiple sclerosis
Although less likely given the presentation, demyelinating disease could present with sensory and motor deficits in the upper extremities.
eliminated: The paresthesias are primarily in the posterior forearm and dorsum of the hand, which is not consistent with median nerve distribution.
